rationale: As a one-portfolio contact sheet, the board reads as 15 silhouettes but only about 8 materially different spatial families. The dominant language is a box/slab chassis with repeated roof or upper-mass tweaks, which makes the portfolio feel family-redundant despite label changes. There are a few promising program-fit moves—especially notch, courtyard, puncture, and lifted threshold—but too many candidates repeat the same footprint, same bar/slab core, or the same stepped roof. For this neighborhood mixed-use program, the board also needs a clearer public void / terrace / split relation and a more explicit active-ground threshold language. The next run should anchor around missing relations that change both section and access: split bridge, carve void, setback, terrace, lift, bent linear mass, courtyard, and a deeper notch.

required_next_relations: Develop one true split-wing composition where the public gap is primary, not decorative, and the ground spine remains occupied and legible from the street.
Introduce one courtyard or carved-void family with a precise public margin and deeper usable exterior room, not just a roof cut.
Add one terrace/setback family with a clearly stepped public pause at the street edge and a calmer upper mass.
Diversify section language: one lifted mass with a genuine undercroft, one notch with strong depth/height proportions, and one bent bar that changes access direction.
Avoid reusing the same rectangular bar/slab chassis; each new candidate should change footprint, section, and threshold logic together.
Keep the ground edge active in all new options so upper experimentation does not erase street engagement.
